prompt_text: I was in a car accident in Pleasanton CA. Which lawyer should I hire for my injury case?
answer_verbatim:
I can help — but to pick the right lawyer I need a few details about your accident and priorities. Meanwhile here’s practical, immediately useful guidance so you can start looking and interviewing attorneys today.

Quick questions that will help me recommend specific lawyers:
- Where exactly in Pleasanton are you located (zip code)?
- When did the accident happen?
- Were you or the other driver insured? Any police report?
- How serious are your injuries and are you still treating?
- Do you want maximum money (including trial) or a fast settlement?
- Any deadline (e.g., employer or insurer demands, lawsuit already filed)?

Important immediate steps (if you haven’t done these)
1. Get medical care and keep records (doctor notes, imaging, bills).  
2. Preserve evidence: photos of vehicles/scene/injuries, the police report number, witness contact info.  
3. Report to your auto insurer as required (give facts; avoid admitting fault).  
4. Don’t post detailed accounts of the crash on social media.  
5. Note deadlines: in California the ordinary personal-injury statute of limitations is 2 years from the date of injury (Code Civ. Proc. §335.1); claims against a public entity require much shorter notice periods (often 6 months). Don’t miss the deadline.

How to choose a lawyer (priorities and red flags)
- Specialization: choose a lawyer who focuses on car-accident/personal-injury work, not a generalist.  
- Experience & results: ask about similar cases, typical settlements/verdicts, trial experience.  
- Local knowledge: Pleasanton/Oakland/Bay Area experience helps (local courts, adjusters, medical providers).  
- Communication: who will handle the case daily (attorney vs paralegal)? How often will they update you?  
- Fee structure: most work on contingency (no fee unless you recover). Typical contingency is ~33% for pre-suit, 33–40% if a suit is filed; ask about costs you might owe if you lose.  
- Resources: complexity (catastrophic injury, multiple parties, uninsured driver) may require a firm with investigators/experts.  
- Red flags: guarantees of outcome, pressure to sign immediately, poor responsiveness, unclear fee agreement, no trial experience for serious claims.

Questions to ask at a free consultation
- Do you handle car-accident cases full-time? How many per year?  
- Have you handled cases like mine (similar injuries/circumstances)? Can you give examples/outcomes?  
- Who will work on my case day-to-day? How do you communicate and how often?  
- What is your fee and what additional costs might I be responsible for?  
- What is your strategy for my case (settlement vs prepare for trial)?  
- How long do you expect this to take? What settlement range is realistic?  
- How do you handle medical liens/subrogation with health insurers/Medicare?  
- Can I see a sample contingency fee agreement?

What to bring to a consultation
- Police report (if available), photos, contact info for other parties/witnesses, insurance info.  
- Medical records/bills and notes about ongoing treatment.  
- Correspondence from insurers or other lawyers.  
- Timeline of what happened and any lost wages.

Typical timeline and costs (very approximate)
- Early investigation and demand package: weeks–months.  
- Settlement negotiations: months, sometimes longer if serious injuries.  
- If suit is filed: 1–3+ years until resolution (varies widely).  
- Costs: contingency fee (commonly ~33%), plus case costs (medical record retrieval, expert fees). Many firms advance costs and recoup them from recovery.

Finding attorneys in Pleasanton
- Ask friends/family for referrals.  
- Check State Bar of California (attorney search), local bar association, and reputable attorney directories (look at reviews and discipline history).  
- Interview 2–4 lawyers and compare answers and comfort level.

If you want, I can:
- Search for and list experienced Pleasanton/Bay Area car-accident attorneys (I’ll need your zip code or willingness to consider nearby cities).  
- Draft a short script/email you can use to contact firms.  
- Help analyze a contingency fee agreement you receive.

Tell me the answers to the quick questions above (or your zip code) and I’ll find a short list of attorneys you can call.
